# MCPower validation — denominator df calibration (mixed models)

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# Run from mcpower/validation/. Reads the frozen study output written by
# df_calibration.R (data/df_calibration.rds); this page renders, it does not
# simulate.
RES <- readRDS(file.path("data", "df_calibration.rds"))
S   <- RES$settings
tab <- RES$table
cur <- RES$curves
png_type <- if (capabilities("cairo")) "cairo" else "Xlib"
pct <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * x))
arm_name <- c(z = "Wald z (asymptotic)", bw = "between-within t", sat = "lmerTest Satterthwaite t")
```

# What this report shows

A mixed-model fixed-effect test needs a reference distribution. On the
single-grouping, random-intercept designs this grid covers, MCPower's default
(`df_method = "auto"`) is a **t with between-within degrees of freedom** (SAS
`DDFM=BETWITHIN`): a
cluster-level predictor is referred to the between-cluster df, an
observation-level predictor to the within-cluster df, and a fit whose
random-effect variances all collapse to zero to the residual df. The
`Denominator df` setting swaps it for the asymptotic **Wald z**. This page
measures how far each choice sits from the nominal 5% when the number of
clusters is small, and what that does to the recommended sample size. The external reference is
**lmerTest's Satterthwaite t** on the same generated data (linear mixed model only —
lmerTest does not fit GLMMs, so the logit cells carry the two MCPower arms only).

Nothing here is a pass/fail gate. The numbers are the evidence for the default
on these designs. They are what moved it from the Wald z to between-within. A
linear mixed model with a random slope, or with crossed or nested groupings, is
tested at per-fit Satterthwaite df under the default instead. The intercept-only
grid does not cover those designs; the random-slope grid at the end of this
page covers single-grouping models with a random slope, against lmerTest,
Kenward–Roger and Wald z.

# What between-within df is

A Wald z treats the standard error of a coefficient as known. In a mixed model
it is not: the standard error of a cluster-level coefficient comes from the
spread of g cluster means, so it carries the uncertainty of g numbers, not of N
observations. With few clusters the z reference is too narrow and the test
rejects too often. The between-within rule (SAS `PROC MIXED`, `DDFM=BETWITHIN`)
refers each fixed effect to a *t* whose denominator df counts the units that
inform it:

- **between df** = g − (number of fixed effects constant within a cluster,
  intercept included). Here the intercept and `z` are cluster-level, so g − 2.
- **within df** = N − g − (number of fixed effects that vary inside clusters).
  Here only `x`, so N − g − 1. The two add up to N − p, the ordinary residual
  df.
- **joint test** of k effects: k·F(k, df) with the smallest df across the
  target set (here g − 2).
- **collapsed fit** (every random-effect variance estimated at zero, lme4's
  "singular fit"): the cluster split no longer describes the fitted model, so
  a linear mixed model fit is referred to Student *t* on N − p and a GLMM fit to
  Wald z.

A predictor counts as cluster-level only when the user declares it (the
cluster-level-variables argument of `set_cluster`); the engine does not detect
it from the data. The rule applies to LMM and clustered GLMM fixed effects
alike: the statistic is the same Wald ratio, only its reference changes.

Satterthwaite df, the lmerTest default, instead estimates the df from how
variable the variance estimate itself is. On a balanced random-intercept design
like this one it gives g − 2 for a cluster-level effect, the same as
between-within. For the within-cluster effect `x` it comes out somewhat above
N − g − 1 (`x` is a random covariate, so part of its variation sits between
clusters); both df are far enough into the tail that the critical values are
practically the same. The tables below show both df columns. Kenward–Roger
also adjusts the standard error and is not part of the intercept-only grid; the
random-slope grid includes it.

# The grid

Every cell fits `y ~ x + z + (1|g)`: `x` varies within clusters, `z` is
constant within a cluster (declared cluster-level). Clusters are balanced with
`r S$cluster_size` observations each, so N = `r S$cluster_size` × g.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Clusters g | `r paste(sort(unique(tab$g)), collapse = ", ")` |
| ICC | `r paste(sort(unique(tab$icc)), collapse = ", ")` |
| Families | `r paste(unique(tab$family), collapse = ", ")` |
| Draws per cell (type-I) | `r format(S$K, big.mark = ",")` |
| Draws per N-grid point (power) | `r format(S$K_N, big.mark = ",")` |
| α | `r S$alpha` |
| Alternative effect | LMM `r S$alt_effect[["lme"]]`; logit `r S$alt_effect[["logit"]]` (log-odds), baseline p = `r S$baseline_p` |
| Versions | mcpower `r S$mcpower`, lmerTest `r S$lmerTest`, lme4 `r S$lme4` |

All arms score the **same generated bytes** per draw: MCPower's own fit gives
the statistic and each arm's critical value; lmerTest refits the identical
design, outcome, and cluster ids. A draw counts only when every arm scored it
(engine converged, lmerTest fit succeeded). The Monte-Carlo standard error on a
5% rate at `r format(S$K, big.mark = ",")` draws is about
`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / S$K))` percentage points.

# Type-I error at effect = 0

Rejection rate at the null, per arm and target. Between-within df for `z` is
g − 2 (intercept and `z` are both cluster-level) and for `x` N − g − 1 on a
live fit. In the linear mixed model a collapsed fit (every random-effect
variance at zero) is referred to the residual df N − 3 on both targets; a
collapsed logit fit falls to Wald z and carries no df. The df columns for the
between-within and Satterthwaite arms are means over draws, so on logit cells
the between-within mean runs over the live draws only. "Collapsed"
is the share of draws whose fit collapsed.

```{r type1-table, results='asis'}
for (fam in unique(tab$family)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", if (fam == "lme") "Linear mixed model" else "Logit GLMM"))
  t <- tab[tab$family == fam, ]
  t <- t[order(t$icc, t$g, t$target, match(t$arm, c("z", "bw", "sat"))), ]
  out <- data.frame(
    ICC = t$icc, g = t$g, N = t$n, target = sprintf("%s (%s)", t$target, t$level),
    arm = arm_name[t$arm], df = ifelse(is.infinite(t$df), "∞", sprintf("%.1f", t$df)),
    `collapsed %` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * t$collapsed_share),
    `type-I %` = pct(t$type1),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%s – %s", pct(t$type1_lo), pct(t$type1_hi)),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "rrrllrrrl"))
  cat("\n")
}
```

```{r type1-plot, results='asis'}
figdir_src <- "figures"
figdir_out <- file.path("..", "web", "documentation", "validation", figdir_src)
dir.create(figdir_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
fpath <- file.path(figdir_out, "df_calibration_type1.png")
fams <- unique(tab$family); iccs <- sort(unique(tab$icc))
grDevices::png(fpath, width = 360 * length(iccs), height = 300 * length(fams), res = 96, type = png_type)
op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(length(fams), length(iccs)), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
cols <- c(z = "#c0392b", bw = "#2874a6", sat = "#1e8449")
for (fam in fams) for (icc in iccs) {
  t <- tab[tab$family == fam & tab$icc == icc, ]
  graphics::plot(NA, xlim = range(t$g), ylim = c(0, max(0.12, max(t$type1_hi, na.rm = TRUE))),
                 xlab = "clusters g", ylab = "type-I error",
                 main = sprintf("%s, ICC %g", if (fam == "lme") "LMM" else "logit GLMM", icc), log = "x")
  graphics::abline(h = 0.05, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  for (arm in unique(t$arm)) for (tg in c("x", "z")) {
    s <- t[t$arm == arm & t$target == tg, ]; s <- s[order(s$g), ]
    graphics::lines(s$g, s$type1, col = cols[arm], lty = if (tg == "z") 1 else 3, lwd = 2)
    graphics::points(s$g, s$type1, col = cols[arm], pch = if (tg == "z") 16 else 1)
  }
}
graphics::legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
                 legend = c(arm_name[unique(tab$arm)], "z (between, solid)", "x (within, dotted)"),
                 col = c(cols[unique(tab$arm)], "black", "black"),
                 lty = c(rep(1, length(unique(tab$arm))), 1, 3), lwd = 2)
graphics::par(op); invisible(grDevices::dev.off())
cat(sprintf("![Type-I error at the null per arm, against the number of clusters. Dashed line: nominal 5%%.](%s)\n\n",
            file.path(figdir_src, "df_calibration_type1.png")))
```

# Joint test of {x, z} at the null

Rejection rate of the joint test of both fixed effects. MCPower's joint Wald
uses a χ²(2) reference under the asymptotic arm and 2·F(2, df_min) under
between-within (df_min = the smallest per-target df in the target set, here
g − 2).
The MCPower rates come from `find_power` on its own draw stream; the lmerTest
joint F (Satterthwaite) is scored on the per-draw refits. Linear mixed model
only.

```{r joint-table, results='asis'}
j <- tab[tab$family == "lme" & tab$target == "x", ]
if (nrow(j)) {
  j <- j[order(j$icc, j$g, match(j$arm, c("z", "bw", "sat"))), ]
  out <- data.frame(ICC = j$icc, g = j$g, N = j$n, arm = arm_name[j$arm],
                    `joint type-I %` = pct(j$joint_type1), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "rrrlr"))
} else cat("*No linear-mixed-model cells in this run.*\n")
```

# Sample size at 80% power

Power at the alternative along an N grid with g held fixed (clusters grow, their
count does not), per arm. "N at 80%" is the first grid point reaching
`r 100 * S$target_power`% power; "—" means no grid point reached it (the grid
tops out at `r max(S$size_grid)` observations per cluster). The grid also has a
floor: its first point is `r min(S$size_grid)` observations per cluster, so an
"N at 80%" equal to g × `r min(S$size_grid)` means power was already above the
target at the smallest N tried, not that this N is the requirement. With few clusters a
cluster-level effect has a power ceiling no cluster size can lift, so "—" on
`z` at small g is the finding, not a grid defect.

```{r n80-table, results='asis'}
for (fam in unique(tab$family)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", if (fam == "lme") "Linear mixed model" else "Logit GLMM"))
  t <- tab[tab$family == fam, ]
  key <- unique(t[, c("icc", "g", "n", "target", "level")])
  key <- key[order(key$icc, key$g, key$target), ]
  arms <- unique(t$arm)
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(key)), function(i) {
    k <- key[i, ]
    pick <- function(arm, col) {
      v <- t[t$icc == k$icc & t$g == k$g & t$target == k$target & t$arm == arm, col]
      if (length(v)) v else NA
    }
    row <- data.frame(ICC = k$icc, g = k$g, N = k$n, target = sprintf("%s (%s)", k$target, k$level),
                      check.names = FALSE)
    for (arm in arms) row[[sprintf("power %% at N, %s", arm)]] <- pct(pick(arm, "power_at_n"))
    for (arm in arms) row[[sprintf("N at 80%%, %s", arm)]] <- {
      v <- pick(arm, "n_at_80"); ifelse(is.na(v), "—", as.character(v)) }
    row
  }))
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "l"))
  cat("\n")
}
```

```{r curves-plot, results='asis'}
fpath <- file.path(figdir_out, "df_calibration_power.png")
gs <- sort(unique(tab$g))
grDevices::png(fpath, width = 300 * length(gs), height = 300 * length(fams), res = 96, type = png_type)
op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(length(fams), length(gs)), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
for (fam in fams) for (g in gs) {
  labs <- unique(tab$label[tab$family == fam & tab$g == g])
  graphics::plot(NA, xlim = range(S$size_grid), ylim = c(0, 1), log = "x",
                 xlab = "observations per cluster", ylab = "power",
                 main = sprintf("%s, g = %d", if (fam == "lme") "LMM" else "logit GLMM", g))
  graphics::abline(h = S$target_power, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  for (lab in labs) {
    c1 <- cur[cur$label == lab, ]; c1 <- c1[order(c1$n), ]
    lwd <- if (grepl("icc0.5", lab)) 2 else 1
    for (arm in c("z", "bw", "sat")) for (tg in c("x", "z")) {
      col <- sprintf("power_%s_%s", arm, tg)
      if (all(is.na(c1[[col]]))) next
      graphics::lines(c1$cluster_size, c1[[col]], col = cols[arm], lwd = lwd, lty = if (tg == "z") 1 else 3)
    }
  }
}
graphics::par(op); invisible(grDevices::dev.off())
cat(sprintf("![Power along the cluster-size grid per arm (colour), target (solid = z between, dotted = x within) and ICC (thin = 0.1, thick = 0.5). Dashed line: 80%%.](%s)\n\n",
            file.path(figdir_src, "df_calibration_power.png")))
```

# Sanity tripwire

Between-within power must never exceed Wald-z power on the same draws (a larger
critical value can only lower it). This is a wiring check, not a calibration
claim.

```{r sanity, results='asis'}
cat(if (isTRUE(RES$sanity_ok))
  "> **OK** — between-within power ≤ Wald-z power on every grid point.\n"
  else "> **VIOLATED** — between-within power exceeded Wald-z power on at least one grid point; the reference-distribution wiring needs a look before reading anything else on this page.\n")
```

# Random-slope designs

```{r slopes-setup}
SL_PATH <- file.path("data", "df_calibration_slopes.rds")
HAVE_SL <- file.exists(SL_PATH)
if (HAVE_SL) {
  SL  <- readRDS(SL_PATH)
  SLS <- SL$settings
  slt <- SL$table
}
sl_arm_name <- c(bw = "between-within t", sat = "MCPower Satterthwaite t (= auto)",
                 z = "Wald z", lmertest = "lmerTest Satterthwaite t", kr = "Kenward–Roger")
sl_arms <- c("bw", "sat", "z", "lmertest", "kr")
```

A linear mixed model with a random slope is tested at per-fit Satterthwaite df
under the default (`df_method = "auto"`). This grid checks that choice where the
intercept-only grid above cannot: on a random-slope target, between-within df
counts the observations inside the clusters, but the effect rests on how many
clusters there are.

Every cell fits `y ~ x * w + (1 + x | g)`. `x` varies within clusters and has a
random slope; `w` is binary and declared cluster-level. The two targets are `x`,
a within-cluster effect with a random slope, and `x:w`, a cross-level
interaction. Both are 0 (the null); `w` = 0.3. The ICC (intercept share) is
`r if (HAVE_SL) SLS$icc`.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Clusters g | `r if (HAVE_SL) paste(SLS$g, collapse = ", ")` |
| Cluster size | `r if (HAVE_SL) paste(SLS$cluster_sizes, collapse = ", ")` |
| Slope variance | `r if (HAVE_SL) paste(SLS$slope_var, collapse = ", ")` |
| Draws per cell, MCPower arms | `r if (HAVE_SL) format(SLS$K, big.mark = ",")` |
| Draws per cell, lmerTest and Kenward–Roger | `r if (HAVE_SL) format(SLS$K_R, big.mark = ",")` (the first ones of the same stream) |
| Kenward–Roger on cluster sizes | `r if (HAVE_SL) paste(SLS$kr_sizes, collapse = ", ")` |
| Versions | mcpower `r if (HAVE_SL) SLS$mcpower`, lmerTest `r if (HAVE_SL) SLS$lmerTest`, lme4 `r if (HAVE_SL) SLS$lme4`, pbkrtest `r if (HAVE_SL) SLS$pbkrtest` |

The arms score the same generated bytes per draw. MCPower fits each draw three
times: between-within, Satterthwaite, and the default. The Wald z arm uses
MCPower's statistic against the normal quantile. lmerTest refits the identical
design matrix, outcome and cluster ids, and Kenward–Roger is computed on that
fit (`pbkrtest`). A draw counts for the MCPower arms when all three MCPower fits
converged. It counts for lmerTest and Kenward–Roger when the lmerTest fit also
succeeded. The default and the Satterthwaite arm differed (in statistic or
critical value) on
`r if (HAVE_SL) sum(slt$auto_neq_sat[!duplicated(slt$label)])` draws over the
whole grid, so one column shows both. The Monte-Carlo SE on a 5% rate is about
`r if (HAVE_SL) sprintf("%.2f", 100 * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / SLS$K))` points at the
MCPower draw count and
`r if (HAVE_SL) sprintf("%.2f", 100 * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / SLS$K_R))` points at
the R draw count.

## Type-I error at effect = 0

Rejection rate in %, per cell, target and arm. "df" is the median Satterthwaite
df of MCPower's fits; "between-within df" is the df that arm used. "Singular"
is the share of draws whose MCPower fit has a random-effect variance at zero or
a correlation at ±1. "MCPower on R draws" gives MCPower's Satterthwaite arm on
exactly the draws lmerTest and Kenward–Roger scored, for a paired comparison.

```{r slopes-type1, results='asis'}
if (!HAVE_SL) {
  cat("*Not run yet: `DFCAL_GRID=slopes Rscript df_calibration.R` writes data/df_calibration_slopes.rds.*\n")
} else {
  for (tg in c("x:w", "x")) {
    cat(sprintf("\n### Target `%s` (%s)\n\n", tg,
                if (tg == "x") "within-cluster, random slope" else "cross-level interaction"))
    t <- slt[slt$target == tg, ]
    keys <- unique(t[, c("g", "cluster_size", "slope_var", "n")])
    keys <- keys[order(keys$cluster_size, keys$slope_var, keys$g), ]
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
      k <- keys[i, ]
      s <- t[t$g == k$g & t$cluster_size == k$cluster_size & t$slope_var == k$slope_var, ]
      v <- function(arm, col) { x <- s[s$arm == arm, col]; if (length(x)) x[1] else NA }
      row <- data.frame(`size` = k$cluster_size, `slope var` = k$slope_var, g = k$g, N = k$n,
                        `between-within df` = sprintf("%.0f", v("bw", "df_median")),
                        df = sprintf("%.1f", v("sat", "df_median")),
                        `singular %` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * v("sat", "singular_share")),
                        check.names = FALSE)
      for (a in sl_arms) row[[sl_arm_name[[a]]]] <- pct(v(a, "type1"))
      row[["MCPower on R draws"]] <- pct(v("sat", "type1_shared"))
      row
    }))
    print(knitr::kable(out, align = "r"))
    cat("\n")
  }
}
```

```{r slopes-plot, results='asis'}
if (HAVE_SL) {
  fpath <- file.path(figdir_out, "df_calibration_slopes_type1.png")
  sizes <- sort(unique(slt$cluster_size)); tgs <- c("x:w", "x")
  vars <- sort(unique(slt$slope_var))
  grDevices::png(fpath, width = 330 * length(vars), height = 290 * length(tgs) * length(sizes),
                 res = 96, type = png_type)
  op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(length(tgs) * length(sizes), length(vars)), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
  scol <- c(bw = "#2874a6", sat = "#1e8449", z = "#c0392b", lmertest = "#7d3c98", kr = "#b9770e")
  for (tg in tgs) for (m in sizes) for (v in vars) {
    t <- slt[slt$target == tg & slt$cluster_size == m & slt$slope_var == v, ]
    graphics::plot(NA, xlim = range(t$g), ylim = c(0, max(0.12, max(t$type1_hi, na.rm = TRUE))), log = "x",
                   xlab = "clusters g", ylab = "type-I error",
                   main = sprintf("%s, size %d, slope var %g", tg, m, v))
    graphics::abline(h = 0.05, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
    for (a in sl_arms) {
      s <- t[t$arm == a & !is.na(t$type1), ]; s <- s[order(s$g), ]
      if (!nrow(s)) next
      graphics::lines(s$g, s$type1, col = scol[[a]], lwd = 2)
      graphics::points(s$g, s$type1, col = scol[[a]], pch = 16)
    }
  }
  graphics::legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, legend = sl_arm_name[sl_arms],
                   col = scol[sl_arms], lwd = 2)
  graphics::par(op); invisible(grDevices::dev.off())
  cat(sprintf("![Random-slope grid: type-I error at the null per arm against the number of clusters, per target, cluster size and slope variance. Dashed line: nominal 5%%.](%s)\n\n",
              file.path(figdir_src, "df_calibration_slopes_type1.png")))
}
```

## Joint test of {x, x:w} at the null

The MCPower rates come from `find_power` on its own draw stream with
`r if (HAVE_SL) format(SLS$K, big.mark = ",")` simulations, as in the
intercept-only grid: 2·F(2, df_min) under between-within and Satterthwaite,
χ²(2) under Wald z. lmerTest's joint F (Satterthwaite) and the Kenward–Roger F
are scored on the per-draw refits.

```{r slopes-joint, results='asis'}
if (HAVE_SL) {
  j <- slt[slt$target == "x", ]
  keys <- unique(j[, c("g", "cluster_size", "slope_var", "n")])
  keys <- keys[order(keys$cluster_size, keys$slope_var, keys$g), ]
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
    k <- keys[i, ]
    s <- j[j$g == k$g & j$cluster_size == k$cluster_size & j$slope_var == k$slope_var, ]
    row <- data.frame(size = k$cluster_size, `slope var` = k$slope_var, g = k$g, N = k$n, check.names = FALSE)
    for (a in c("bw", "sat", "auto", "z", "lmertest", "kr"))
      row[[if (a == "auto") "MCPower default" else sl_arm_name[[a]]]] <- pct(s$joint_type1[s$arm == a][1])
    row
  }))
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "r"))
}
```

## Run record (random-slope grid)

```{r slopes-record, results='asis'}
if (HAVE_SL) {
  first <- slt[!duplicated(slt$label), ]
  cat(sprintf("Frozen output of `DFCAL_GRID=slopes validation/df_calibration.R`, last run %s, wall time %.0f s for the cells this run computed. Draws without three converged MCPower fits, per cell (of %s): %s. Draws among the first %s with converged MCPower fits but no usable lmerTest fit: %s. Draws whose Satterthwaite pass failed (tested at Wald z by MCPower), per cell and target x / x:w: %s.\n",
              SLS$run_at, SLS$elapsed_sec, format(SLS$K, big.mark = ","),
              paste(sprintf("%s %d", first$label, first$skipped), collapse = "; "),
              format(SLS$K_R, big.mark = ","),
              paste(sprintf("%s %d", first$label, first$r_skipped), collapse = "; "),
              paste(vapply(first$label, function(l) {
                s <- slt[slt$label == l & slt$arm == "sat", ]
                sprintf("%s %d/%d", l, s$df_fallback[s$target == "x"], s$df_fallback[s$target == "x:w"])
              }, ""), collapse = "; ")))
}
```

# Run record (intercept-only grid)

Frozen output of `validation/df_calibration.R`, last run `r S$run_at`, wall
time `r sprintf("%.0f", S$elapsed_sec)` s for the cells this run computed;
cells resumed from an earlier run's checkpoint (same seeds and settings, which
the checkpoint guard checks) are not in that wall time. Draws skipped (non-converged engine fit
or failed lmerTest fit) per cell: `r paste(sprintf("%s %d", unique(tab$label), tab$skipped[!duplicated(tab$label)]), collapse = "; ")`.
